Section 01 · 5 min
The Origin Story
I was sitting in the dark, holding a cow.
I manage anxiety. My nervous system has always needed a little more than the world typically offers — more weight, more movement, more sensation, more time.
A long performance. A vibration device on my ankle, keeping me regulated. Norman — then just a Highland Cow plush — in my lap.
The thought that came in the dark has a name — co-regulation. When we hold someone we love, our nervous systems synchronize.
I went home and started building. The moment I squeezed the first prototype and felt it vibrate back, something clicked. It answered me.
I wrote to the cow's makers to share the idea. Then I realized — this wasn't a suggestion. This was mine to build.
"What if Norman could do this too? What if squeezing him meant feeling vibration back?"
Not from a product brief or a market gap analysis. From a dark theater, a Highland Cow, and a nervous system that needed something that didn't exist yet.

Section 02 · 5 min
Meet Norman
A Highland Cow stuffed animal with vibration motors, a pressure sensor, RGB LED button, and wireless charging built inside. Four therapeutic modes.
  • Responsive Hug — squeeze Norman, he vibrates back. Squeeze harder, feel more.
  • Heartbeat — a lub-dub that slows from 32→22 BPM over 5 minutes
  • Deep Calm — a wave that travels M1→M2→M3 and fades over 10 minutes
  • Box Breathing — a Gaussian wave guides your inhale and exhale

The Heart of It
Building with
an AI Design Team
Every discipline. One designer. A team of AIs.
Section 03 · Act 1
AI as Assistant
In the beginning, I used AI the way most designers do — as a very smart search engine and helper. I asked questions. I got answers. I learned fast.
  • Debugging firmware I didn't fully understand
  • Researching trademarks and prior art
  • Understanding haptic motor specifications
  • Generating first-draft copy I could react to
  • Explaining circuits and components in plain language
The early questions
I'm a designer with no engineering background. What does an Arduino actually do?
What kind of sensor could tell a stuffed animal it's being squeezed?
My motor just buzzes constantly — how do I make it pulse like a heartbeat?
Great question! Let's start with…
The shift
"I went from asking questions to having a conversation."

Section 03 · Act 2 · Continued
Beyond the studio
The same collaborator, wearing different hats — the business departments no solo designer has.
Dept · Legal
  • Patent research and prior-art scans — I walked into attorney consults knowing the questions
  • Trademark research on the names we chose, before filing
Dept · Manufacturing
  • Component sourcing and BOM decisions — boards, motors, batteries, charging
  • Research on paths from hand-built to producible
Dept · User Research
  • Turned early tester feedback into reference guides — How to Hold Norman, When to Reach for Norman
  • Grounded the modes in co-regulation and nervous-system research
Dept · Product
  • The layer around the plush — Norm's Modes hang tag, quick start guide, care instructions
  • Naming, packaging language, and the small decisions that make it feel real
Claude
Section 03 · Act 3
AI in the Environment
The final shift: the AI moved into my environment.
BEFORE
Claude in a browser tab. Me, copy-pasting code into the Arduino IDE, pasting errors back — one round-trip at a time.
AFTER
Claude as the architect. Claude Code as the developing partner — inside VS Code, reading the whole project, writing and running the firmware with me.
The new org chart
Claude became my architect — deciding what to build and why. Claude Code became my engineer — building it in VS Code. I sat between them as the director, carrying decisions from one to the other.

What it unlocked · the haptic wavelengths

"It stopped feeling like a tool and started feeling like a collaborator who was actually in the room."

The Empowering Part
What AI
Can't Do
Here's what makes you irreplaceable.
Section 04
Five moments AI couldn't save me
The LED
The purple button kept rendering magenta. Claude gave me RGB values. Still wrong. The final value came from me looking at it with my own eyes and saying not yet.
No AI can see your hardware. Calibration requires a human in the room.
The heartbeat
Claude coded the BPM ramp. But whether the lub-dub felt like a heartbeat — I held Norman against my sternum and said yes or no until it was right.
Embodied experience is irreplaceable. You have to feel it.
The tagline
"Embrace your calm" didn't come from a brainstorm. It came from lying in bed one night with Norman in my arms.
Insight lives in the quiet. AI doesn't have quiet.
The leather
Nobody told me to add a leather heart as the squeeze indicator. That came from my hands — from knowing what tactile warmth feels like.
Craft knowledge is embodied. It doesn't transfer through a chat window.
The hybrid motor decision
When I realized LRA motors were wrong for some modes — that wasn't a logical conclusion. I held the device, felt the difference, and knew.
AI helped me execute it. The instinct was mine.
"AI made me faster, broader, and more capable. But it made me more of a designer. Not less of one."
